summary:
NASA’s Space-Time Capsule: The Hardware We Left Behind

Since the 1960s, NASA spacecraft have explored the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Some have stopped working, some still send data, and others are continuing their journeys through deep space. This project tells the stories of these machines: what they were built to do, what they discovered, and what their journeys can teach us about exploring safely and thoughtfully
details: Our project is a youth-friendly guide to NASA hardware left across the solar system. It features Moon landers and experiments, Mars rovers, and deep-space probes. Each story explains where the machine went, what it was designed to do, what it helped scientists discover, and whether it still works. The guide shows that “left behind” equipment has many different stories. Some machines completed their missions after making important discoveries. Others stopped working, while a few still send data from far away. Simple profiles, diagrams, and a solar-system map help young readers see how engineering choices—such as power, communication, and durability—shape what scientists can learn. Our goal is to spark curiosity about space science and engineering. We’ll use clear, age-appropriate language and consider accuracy, accessibility, and the effects of leaving equipment on other worlds.
